question.knowledge_point: Representing a Double Integral as a Repeated Integral When the Limits are Given
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14100085/assets/0e05b575c22c78000a1ec235bb82cbfad3cd0cdfc6db370f19f094799b305949.png)

If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y=2{x}^{2}$ and $y=1+{x}^{2},$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14100085/assets/da2895c09bc33f628626257b6d102e74875825df14ba744904e02ffa71552a02.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,2{x}^{2}\le y\le 1+{x}^{2}\}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{2{x}^{2}}^{1+{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{2{x}^{2}}^{1+{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\,dy]dx\end{aligned}
$$
